title: Empire even over reigning Christ—old rhythmic prose and Paris Missal: ‘by mother’s right command the Redeemer’
source_text: LXIV. Neque tantum creaturas omnes Virgini tanquam Dominae proprie dictae subjiciunt, sed etiam imperium & authoritatem illi tribuunt in ipsum Christum jam gloriose in coelo Regnantem. Quo spectat vetus illa prosa Rhythmica, a nostris saepius citata, Gaude Matrona caelica, Tu ancillam Jesu Christi, Te vocare noli, Sed ut docet lex divina, Tu illius es Domina. Nam lex docet & ratio; Matrem praeesse Filio. Ergo ora suppliciter, Et praecipe sublimiter, Ut nos in mundi Vespere, Ad regna ducat suprema. Quibus concinunt illa veteri Missali Parisiensi inserta, O felix puerpera, Nostra pians scelera, Jure matris impera Redemptori.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do they subject only all creatures to the Virgin as Lady properly so called, but they also attribute to her empire and authority over Christ Himself now gloriously Reigning in heaven. To which looks that old rhythmic prose, often cited by our men: Rejoice, heavenly Matron; Do not will to call thyself handmaid of Jesus Christ, But as the divine law teaches, Thou art His Lady. For law and reason teach that the Mother is set over the Son. Therefore pray as a suppliant, And command from on high, That in the world’s Evening He lead us to the highest kingdoms. With which agree those things inserted in the old Paris Missal: O happy childbearer, Atoning our crimes, By mother’s right command the Redeemer.
pass_b_english: They claim empire not only over creatures but over Christ reigning in glory.
Old rhythmic prose and Paris Missal: mother stands over the Son—‘by mother’s right command the Redeemer.’
